notes: Discriminating assertions are the evidence and path:line ones; the 'no defensive checks' and 'no length split' assertions passed in all six runs and don't separate the configurations.

Both configurations found every seeded defect. The skill's gain is evidence quality: it ran the assert side effect in scratch (3 vs 2), counted call sites, and estimated the line/column rescan cost; the baseline restated rules in several findings.
Accuracy: the small-commit baseline made two false claims (call-site count, store routing); the with-skill runs had one minor error each, in non-finding sections.

Coverage gap: only the medium baseline noticed that the Chibi parser and tokenizer selectors are in no CI group in tools/test_policy.py. The skill has no check for 'is the new or touched test actually run by CI'.
The seeded with-skill run put the string-compared node kind under 'leave alone' with a correct reason (the forest stores kinds as strings by design); assertion 4 was too strict.
Cost: the skill used about 29% more tokens and 42% more time on average (one run each, so variance is unknown).
